subject: Climate & Environment
title: Trees as Carbon Machines
description: A tiny lesson with a big payoff: Trees as Carbon Machines.

hook.text: A single mature tree absorbs about 22 kilograms of CO₂ per year and locks it in wood.

buildup.text: Leaves pull CO₂ from the air. Photosynthesis splits it into carbon and oxygen.

discovery.text: The carbon becomes trunk, branches, and roots. The oxygen goes back into the atmosphere.

twist.text: Forests store more carbon than the entire atmosphere holds as CO₂ right now.

climax.text: When a tree dies naturally, it releases carbon slowly — over decades, not seconds.

punchline.text: Every tree is a slow-motion carbon vault powered by sunlight.

quiz.question: How much CO₂ does a single mature tree absorb per year?

details.summary: Trees absorb CO2 through photosynthesis and store it as wood, making them the most important terrestrial carbon sink. A mature tree can absorb roughly 22 kilograms of CO2 per year, and the world's forests collectively store about 860 billion tons of carbon.
details.whyItMatters: Trees are the cheapest and most proven carbon removal technology available. Every tree cut releases stored carbon; every tree planted begins accumulating it.
takeaways: Forests store roughly 860 billion tons of carbon in biomass and soil
Old-growth trees store the most carbon and continue absorbing more
Deforestation reverses centuries of carbon accumulation in months

faq.question: Do old trees store more carbon than young trees?
faq.answer: Yes. While young trees grow faster in percentage terms, old-growth trees have far more biomass and continue adding carbon each year. A single large tree can store tons of carbon that would take a sapling decades to match.

faq.question: How much carbon can tree planting remove from the atmosphere?
faq.answer: Estimates suggest reforestation could remove 5 to 10 billion tons of CO2 per year at scale, roughly a fifth of annual emissions. However, it takes decades for new forests to reach meaningful carbon storage, so planting cannot substitute for cutting emissions now.
